name: WPForms
summary: Drag-and-drop form builder plugin for WordPress: contact, lead and payment forms from templates, with email, CRM and payment integrations and a free Lite version.
best_for: WordPress site owners and small agencies that want a drag-and-drop form builder with templates, integrations and, on higher plans, payment forms
skip_if: you do not use WordPress, you want a flat price that does not double at renewal, or you only need one simple contact form that the free version covers
honest_knock: The prices on the pricing page are introductory: every plan renews at double the displayed price, and no end date for the introductory offer is given. A licence covers a fixed number of sites (1, 3, 5 or unlimited). Payment add-ons sit on the higher plans, and the free version or an inactive licence adds a 3% platform fee on payments.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · per year, Basic introductory price for the first year, 1 site
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-05 on wpforms.com/pricing) WPForms sells yearly licences for WordPress, by the number of sites. The licence is priced by how many sites you run: $49.50 a year for one site (Basic), $99.50 for three (Plus), $199.50 for five (Pro) and $299.50 for unlimited sites (Elite). Those are "special introductory pricing" shown as 50% off the normal prices of $99, $199, $399 and $599 a year, and the page states that all renewals are at full price. Every plan has unlimited forms, submissions and users, and a 14-day money-back guarantee. Stripe, Square, PayPal and other payment add-ons sit on the higher plans, and the pricing page says a 3% platform fee applies to payments when you use the free version or an inactive licence. All pricing is in USD and you can change plans or cancel at any time. WPForms Lite is free. The introductory price is shown without an end date, so we do not know how long it stays.
